title: Contrail compliance notes — quick control skeleton (Gita)
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for control mapping, early hypotheses and evidence buckets. Not polished — intentional shorthand. Goal: turn this into a minimal control matrix for intake into the repo and then a short checklist for engineering owners.

Topline: we have surface coverage for logging, access, patching, and incident response. Gaps feel concentrated around: delegated admin approvals, ephemeral creds rotation, and proof that autoscale instances are included in patch runs.

Scope: hosted API + dedicated pools + private deployables (VPC). Focus initial pass on infra & platform controls that commonly map to SOC-type criteria: logical access, change management, monitoring, incident management.

Quick control skeleton (id | name | short description | evidence bucket | confidence 0-3):
- CTRL-ACCESS-01 | Admin console access gating | RBAC + SCIM group sync to Okta; MFA required for admin groups | evidence: SCIM config export, Okta group membership, admin login audit | confidence: 2
- CTRL-CRED-02 | Service credentials lifecycle | KMS-backed service keys; rotation policy but many legacy tokens in vault paths | evidence: KMS policy doc, vault list snapshots, rotation run logs | confidence: 1
- CTRL-PATCH-03 | Host/instance patch management | Fleet patch jobs via Ansible + scheduled windows; Dedicated GPU pools sometimes on different cadence | evidence: runbook, patch job history, dedicated-pool tag query | confidence: 1
- CTRL-CHANGE-04 | PR + CI gating for infra changes | Terraform + policy-as-code checks that block prod plan apply without approvals | evidence: sample PRs, policy test runs, audit log of applies | confidence: 2
- CTRL-LOG-05 | Centralized logging and retention | Logs forwarded to ELK and backed up; retention policy 90d for infra, 365d for security events | evidence: ELK index mappings, retention configs, daily delivery receipts | confidence: 2
- CTRL-IR-06 | Incident runbook and comms | PagerDuty + incident templates, postmortem cadence 72h | evidence: PD escalation policy, recent postmortem links | confidence: 2

Open questions / probes (to check before finalizing mapping):
1) Are all dedicated GPU pool hosts (including ephemeral burst nodes) enrolled in the same patch job? Who owns the tagging? (owner candidate: infra-eng)
2) Where are long-lived machine tokens stored? Are any in plaintext GH repos or archived S3 objects? (ownership: platform-engineering; urgent)
3) SCIM -> Okta sync: do we have a documented schedule and reconciliation report? How often are stale admin accounts removed? (owner: devops/security)
4) Audit logs: do we have immutable export for prod-admin actions older than 90 days? If not, this is a likely gap for evidence continuity.

Hypotheses (quick):
- H1: Patch coverage is high for core infra but misses ephemeral/dedicated burst nodes because those are provisioned by a different automation pipeline.
- H2: Credential rotation exists for primary services but legacy tokens for older pipelines remain; evidence may be scattered across a few vault paths.
- H3: Change approvals exist in principle but enforcement gaps stem from bypassed CI policies for service accounts tied to infra automation.

Evidence hunting checklist (first pass):
- Export Okta SCIM app config + last sync timestamp (console -> download)
- Run vault path inventory for any tokens with last-used > 90 days; get owner tag for each
- Query patch-job history for nodes with tag:dedicated-pool and tag:burst=true for past 6 months
- Pull sample Terraform apply history for last 3 months, highlight any applies performed by automation service accounts
- Grab ELK index retention config and a sample of security indices older than 90 days (is export present?)

Slack anchors / quick queries to run:
- @infra-engineering: how are dedicated GPU nodes tagged at provisioning? sample terraform module?
- @platform-sre: show me the last inventory of vault paths and which teams own them
- trust-ops-thread: add postmortem links for last 3 incidents with security impact tag

Draft mapping notes (to SOC style criteria, rough):
- Logical Access: CTRL-ACCESS-01 -> maps to CC6.X (access control) & CC7.X (auth)
- System Operations: CTRL-PATCH-03 + CTRL-CHANGE-04 -> maps to CC5.X (change mgmt)
- Monitoring & Logging: CTRL-LOG-05 -> maps to CC4.X (monitoring, detection)
- Incident Mgmt: CTRL-IR-06 -> maps to CC8.X (incident response)
- Encryption & Keys: CTRL-CRED-02 -> maps to CC9.X (cryptographic controls)

Risk questions to include in matrix (short form):
- What is the mean time to revoke a compromised service token? (measureable?)
- How often are privileged groups reviewed and by whom? (evidence: attestation)
- Is there a documented chain of custody for artifacts used to remediate incidents?

Immediate next steps (priority order):
1) Send the evidence checklist to Ben and Sana and ask them to pull: Okta export, vault path inventory, patch job query by 2026-03-12.
2) I will draft a one-page control mapping table from this scratch and push to CONFLUENCE-INFRA-924 as the initial artifact.
3) Book 30m with infra-eng to confirm dedicated pool tagging and patch cadence (owner: Gita)

Notes-to-self / fragments:
- Keep contrail metaphor: "what trails are left after a deploy?" i.e., leftover tokens, ephemeral hosts, untagged images. Good conversation starter with infra.
- Not all evidence needs to be perfect for an internal readiness check; just need reproducible queries and a responsible owner.
- Avoid promising blanket coverage; call out assumptions explicitly in final matrix.

Rough timeline: internal readiness review by 2026-03-18, then iterate for external audit prep if needed.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to tidy matrix once owners reply.
